headline: The drinks index.
notes: Place the serving photograph on the red half and leave two clear choices beside the masthead. The pack route in V1 leads to a shareable pair.
detail: Explore six Singapore drinks by flavour or compare the sizes of two packs.

headline: Leaf or blossom?
notes: Set tall leaf and blossom photographs in staggered arches. Use the caption beneath each print as the direct link to its botanical profile.
detail: Follow first-harvest tea buds or Hang Bai Ju chrysanthemums into the tea house.

headline: The soy study.
notes: Align the labels on the light and dark specimen plates so four pack formats and two pack formats can be read across one line. Carry that pair into V1.
detail: Soy Bean Milk comes in four listed packs. Black Soy Milk comes in two.

headline: On the board.
notes: Keep the six native menu disclosures in reading order and tie the angled counter photograph to whichever drink the visitor opens.
detail: Choose a line on the board to see the drink, its ingredients and its pack sizes.

headline: Find a pack.
notes: Treat the selected matrix column as the source of the oversized coverage fraction. Keep the total and proportional bar immediately above the table.
detail: Choose a format to see how many of the six drinks are offered in it.

headline: Botanical notes.
notes: Use three adjacent crop windows as a photographic specimen key. Each window opens and bookmarks the actual ingredient disclosure.
detail: Trace a flower, a leaf or a bean to its drink profile.

headline: Lychee season.
notes: Keep the circular serving portrait above a measurement strip. Use one common 1,500 mL scale for the four pack capacities.
detail: See how a 250 mL carton compares with a 300 mL can and the two bottle sizes.

headline: Rose milk studio.
notes: Use the serving plate as an ingredient viewfinder. A rose selection crops toward the petals, milk crops into the glass and Together restores the full print.
detail: Look closely at the rose essence and creamy milk behind Bandung.

headline: The Nanyang archive.
notes: Run a two-rule newspaper masthead across the page. Separate the historical lead from the photograph of today's Soy Bean Milk with a vertical column rule.
detail: Follow the business from its beginnings in Zhangzhou to Nanyang in the 1930s.

headline: Picnic counter.
notes: Frame the quantity as a packing slip against the gingham sheet. Put the number and container first, followed by the unit capacity and spare volume.
detail: Enter your guest count and portion size to round the shopping list up to whole packs.

headline: Cooler shelf.
notes: Treat capacity labels as removable shelf tickets. Filtering the cabinet hides both incompatible drinks and incompatible tickets on the cards that remain.
detail: Find the listed drinks and sizes for a carton, can or bottle.

headline: Tasting notebook.
notes: Stamp the selected serving photograph beside its printed drink name in the notebook margin. A flight can open the correct drink's page directly.
detail: Record aroma, texture and finish in a note saved on this device.

headline: The drink dial.
notes: Use the six positions as real profile links. The centre photograph and the printed readout follow keyboard focus as well as the pointer.
detail: Preview a flavour direction, then open the matching drink profile.

headline: Tasting flight.
notes: Join the three pour cards on one continuous strip with tear lines between servings. Give every pour its own route to a matching notebook entry.
detail: Try a sequence of three drinks and record a note for a particular pour.

headline: Beverage atlas.
notes: Give the masthead a labelled search slot. Keep its filtered letter rail aligned with the surviving entries and place the result count by the query.
detail: Look up a drink by name, ingredient or the wording of a pack size.

headline: Six drinks, one index.
notes: An alternate index could place the three featured serving studies in a contact-sheet rail. Selecting a frame would move the profile link to that drink.
detail: Start with a serving photograph and open the drink behind it.

headline: Measure the pack range.
notes: An alternate pack finder could organise the five sizes on a ruled measuring scale. The selected tick would isolate the matching column and retain drink names.
detail: Read the five Singapore pack formats from 250 mL to 1.5 L.

headline: Rose, milk, Bandung.
notes: An alternate ingredient studio could pair three broad colour fields with the existing rose, milk and finished-drink controls, using one serving image throughout.
detail: Select a component to examine the role it plays in the drink.

headline: Pack for the picnic.
notes: An alternate calculator could make the whole-pack result the central parcel label. Keep guest count and serving volume on the stub beside it.
detail: Work from your planned serving volume to the number of individual packs.

headline: From Zhangzhou to Nanyang.
notes: An alternate chronology could lay the two historical milestones on a simple route line and end at the present-day product entry. Distinguish a modern serving photograph from archival evidence.
detail: Read the 1901 founding and the family business’s move to Nanyang in the 1930s.
